decisions.statement: A message counted is a message Alan typed or queued rather than a message an agent sent.
A transcript belongs to the persona whose seat page a read answered that transcript with.
A transcript answered no seat page is read off the persona that transcript is told to be.
A transcript told neither is read off the name Alan greeted.
The first name a transcript has is the name that transcript is held by.
A name quoted inside another message is no name the transcript has.
A transcript answering to no name is counted against nobody.
A name no persona is filed under is passed over rather than counted.
The day a message falls on turns at six in the morning in New York.
A day's counts are replaced by the counts the transcripts say rather than added to.
A day the transcripts say nothing about keeps the counts that day already had.
The personas on a day sit in the order of their names.
A message Alan wrote on another machine is counted nowhere.
A transcript no longer on this machine takes its messages out of the counts.
Nothing here turns a count into points.
Nothing here writes a day page that is not there.
A seat page in a transcript is named by its file rather than by the folder it sits in.

definition: each day's counts built again out of the Claude transcripts on this machine
